# Happy Downloader

> A self-hosted web UI for yt-dlp: one static Go binary with an embedded React
> frontend, built for a headless host that has no browser of its own.

Happy Downloader (欢喜下载) lets a browser anywhere on the LAN queue downloads
that run on a server. It exists because the usual yt-dlp GUI assumes the machine
doing the downloading is the machine you are sitting at. Here it is not: the
server has no desktop session, so cookies have to arrive as a file from
somewhere else, and the interface has to work over the network.

The project is a fork of [marcopeocchi/yt-dlp-web-ui](https://github.com/marcopeocchi/yt-dlp-web-ui).
It is not a wrapper around a CLI; the server builds the yt-dlp argument list
itself, logs it in full, and runs it.

## Key facts

- Language and stack: Go backend (`net/http` + chi), React 18 + MUI + Vite
  frontend, embedded into the binary with `go:embed`. No Node runtime in
  production, no database server — state lives in BoltDB.
- Module path: `github.com/LeisureLinux/happy-downloader/v4`
- Licence: GPL-3.0-only, inherited from upstream. The original copyright is
  preserved; this is not a permissive-licence project.
- Single binary, listens on `0.0.0.0:3033` by default.
- Configured by one YAML file (`-conf`), overridable by `APP_*` environment
  variables with dots replaced by underscores.

## Behaviour worth knowing before changing it

- **Every yt-dlp invocation passes `--ignore-config`.** The host's own yt-dlp
  config must not affect a download, so the logged argv is the complete truth.
  Proxy and PO Token settings are therefore composed explicitly by the server,
  falling back to the global config when a site profile does not override them.
- **Cookie files are converted and watched, not uploaded per request.** A JSON
  export from a browser extension and a Netscape `cookies.txt` are both
  accepted; the format is detected from the content. `httpOnly` is preserved.
- **Each invocation gets its own temporary copy of the cookie jar.** `--cookies`
  also writes back, so a shared path lets one process truncate a file another is
  reading.
- **The download list is a queue, not a history.** Completed downloads are not
  listed; they appear in the file browser instead.
- **A finished probe is cached for ten minutes** so pressing "start" does not
  repeat the metadata extraction the probe just performed.
- **Arguments are validated against an allowlist** before they reach the
  process, and the output path is checked to stay inside the download directory.

  config with WebSocket upgrade and SSE buffering disabled.
- [packaging/systemd/](packaging/systemd/): user units and the cookie refresh
  timer.
- [scripts/refresh-cookies.sh](scripts/refresh-cookies.sh): read a browser
  profile, filter to chosen sites, push the export to the server.


## Installing it for someone

This is a Go binary that shells out to four other things. The binary is the easy
part; the four are where installations fail. Order matters.

1. **yt-dlp in its own venv**, not `apt install yt-dlp` (stale for months) and
   not `pip install --user` (collides with distribution packages).
   `python3 -m venv .../venv && .../venv/bin/pip install -U yt-dlp`.
2. **A JavaScript runtime, node 20+.** yt-dlp needs it to solve YouTube's `n`
   challenge. Without it YouTube returns images only, and the error
   (`Requested format is not available`) does not mention the runtime at all.
3. **A PO Token provider — both halves.** `pip install -U
   bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider` installs the yt-dlp plugin; the token generator is
   a separate Node server cloned from
   github.com/Brainicism/bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider, built with `npm install &&
   npx tsc`, run as `node build/main.js --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4416`. Installing
   only the plugin produces "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" with no hint
   that a second process is missing.
4. **A cookie export from a machine with a browser.** The server cannot log in
   and cannot read a browser profile. Accepts a JSON export or a Netscape
   cookies.txt; the format is detected. The file is watched, so replacing it
   refreshes the session without a restart.
5. **Then the binary**, with every path in config absolute — a user service
   starts in the home directory, so relative paths land somewhere unexpected.

Verify with the full argument line, not one flag at a time. Without a PO Token
provider, yt-dlp now fails on most YouTube videos with "Only images are
available" or "Requested format is not available" — errors that name none of
the missing pieces, so a partial command fails on a working installation and
sends you hunting a fault that is not there. The complete line (cookies, js
runtimes, extractor-args, remote-components) passes only when all four parts
are in place, which is the question being asked:

    yt-dlp --cookies <file> --js-runtimes node:/usr/bin/node \
      --extractor-args 'youtubepot-bgutilhttp:base_url=http://127.0.0.1:4416' \
      --remote-components ejs:github --print '%(title)s | %(ext)s' <url>

Then `curl /api/v1/version` and a `Service.Exec` call through `/rpc/http`.

Two traps that pass a superficial check:

- A guest cookie export still contains `LOGIN_INFO`, so "the file has cookies"
  is not evidence of a session. Verify by resolving a title.
- `--browser chrome` alone can silently fail to decrypt v11 cookies when the
  keyring backend is unrecognised; the export still looks plausible but holds
  ~170 cookies instead of a few thousand. Pass `chrome+gnomekeyring`.

Failure messages map one-to-one to causes: "not a bot" means cookies; "format
not available" or "only images" means PO Token or JS runtime; "n challenge
solving failed" means the runtime is missing or older than 20; timeouts mean the
host cannot reach YouTube and needs `ytdlp.proxy`.

## Configuration

Top-level keys of the config file, all optional:

- `server`: `host`, `port`, `base_url`, `queue_size`
- `paths`: `download_path`, `downloader_path`, `local_database_path`,
  `js_runtime_path`, `cookie_path`
- `ytdlp`: `pot_base_url` (bgutil PO Token provider), `proxy`
- `logging`: `log_path`, `enable_file_logging`

Per-site overrides (proxy, cookie file, extra arguments, PO Token URL) are stored
in the local database and edited from the Settings page, not in this file.

## HTTP surface

JSON-RPC at `POST /rpc/http` carries most operations; `/rpc/ws` streams live
state. Plain endpoints: `/api/v1/version`, `/api/v1/cookies/status`,
`/api/v1/profiles`, `/filebrowser/{downloaded,delete,d/{id},v/{id},bulk}`,
`/log/sse`, `/log/ws`, `/status`. OpenAPI is served at `/openapi`.

## Dependencies

The binary bundles the frontend and nothing else. It shells out for all
downloading, so these live on the host and are updated independently:

- [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) — required; not bundled, because
  YouTube breaks old versions and the fix should not require rebuilding this.
- node 20+ — required for YouTube; yt-dlp uses it for the `n` challenge.
- [bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider](https://github.com/Brainicism/bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider)
  — required for YouTube now; two halves (a venv plugin and a Node server).
- ffmpeg — required unless every download is a single stream.

On a network where YouTube is unreachable directly (poisoned DNS, blocked range),
set `ytdlp.proxy`. The server passes `--proxy` on every invocation and carries
the same value into the PO Token provider's extractor-args, which has no proxy
flag of its own. Test with `curl -sI https://www.youtube.com`; `000` or a reset
means a proxy is not optional.
